_status: PARTIAL: 4 of 5 providers have a detection pattern at all; 2 of those 4 have live validation (docs/DECISIONS.md item 97). Real patterns added Week 7 Batch 4. Schema: id, provider, pattern, known_placeholders (excluded from findings), live_validation (bool), validation_endpoint (informational, matches credential_validation_allowlist's own external_apis entries), gap_reason (live_validation=false entries only). Stripe and Google Maps have live_validation=true (single-value GET-based checks, safely implementable). AWS and Twilio have live_validation=false, each with its own gap_reason. MICROSOFT GRAPH HAS NO PATTERN ENTRY AT ALL -- checked, not guessed: Microsoft's own Sensitive Information Type definition for this credential class describes only a broad character set ('up to 40 characters' of [-_.~a-zA-Z0-9]), and a gitleaks maintainer thread (Oct 2024, github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks/issues/1554) confirms the wider secret-scanning community has not converged on a sufficiently specific regex either -- an early draft of this file used a pattern with a literal '8Q~' substring requirement, apparently a garbled half-memory of Microsoft's own illustrative example value ('abc7Q~defgh...'), not a real structural signature; caught by checking the actual current documentation before trusting it, not shipped. Rather than ship a broad, high-false-positive pattern with a vague caveat, Graph credential detection is left out entirely pending a keyword-proximity heuristic (e.g. requiring the match to appear near 'client_secret') this file doesn't implement yet -- see hardcoded_credentials.py module docstring.

patterns.gap_reason: Requires AWS SigV4 request signing AND a paired secret access key -- a single regex match on an access key ID alone cannot authenticate a request.
Requires a paired Auth Token located near the Account SID in the same JS -- a 'find related values together' pattern this file's simple per-pattern regex scan doesn't attempt.
